summary: Dominica's visa-exemption list lets citizens of the US, the Commonwealth, CARICOM and several EU countries visit for up to six months, and those of the UK, France, Germany, China and some twenty others for up to three; any other bona fide tourist with a return ticket may stay up to 21 days without a visa, and a visitor visa is needed beyond that.

RU.notes: Russian citizens holding any valid passport may enter and stay without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the Russia–Dominica visa-waiver agreement, in force since 14 January 2019. A longer stay, work or business needs a visa from a Dominica mission. The Government of Dominica's own exemption page does not list Russia, and on it alone a Russian visitor would get only the 21-day bona fide tourist allowance.

fee.notes: The government's page states an application fee of $200.00, paid at the Treasury Department in Roseau; it does not name the currency, and Dominican government fees are charged in Eastern Caribbean dollars. Applicants also supply a bank statement and invitation letter from their sponsor, a medical certificate and notarised documents.

declarations.text: Complete the Online Immigration and Customs Declaration (ED) card at edcard.dominica.gov.dm, no more than three days before travel. Save or print the confirmation with its QR code and show it with your passport at the port of entry when asked.

currencyLimits.text: The customs declaration on Dominica's online ED card asks every arriving traveller whether they are carrying currency or monetary instruments over USD 10,000 or the equivalent, and says failure to make a full declaration is an offence that can result in seizure of the goods, fines and/or imprisonment.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says there are strict rules about goods you can take into or out of Dominica, and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

The Government of Canada notes that customs may enforce strict regulations on the import or export of certain items, including business equipment, food and beverages, and chemicals. It is illegal for anyone, including children, to wear camouflage clothing or carry items made of camouflage material.

payments.text: No official source describes how widely cards are accepted in Dominica. The Government of Canada says the currency is the East Caribbean dollar and that many businesses also accept US dollars and euros; the UK Foreign Office says taxi fares can usually be paid in US dollars. Medical facilities may require immediate cash payment.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says the crime rate in Dominica is low, but you could be at risk walking alone away from the main roads, particularly after dark. Canada's travel advice says petty crime such as pickpocketing, purse snatching and theft from vehicles occurs, and that crime typically increases during Carnival and the World Creole Music Festival. The hurricane season runs from June to November.

tips.text: Traffic drives on the left. The Government of Canada says visitors must buy a temporary Dominican driving permit, valid for 30 days, available at the airports, car rental firms, the Traffic and Licensing Department on High Street in Roseau and the Portsmouth Police Station. The UK Foreign Office warns that roads are sometimes narrow and in poor condition.

The Government of Canada advises never hiking alone, hiring an experienced guide from a reputable company, staying informed about the weather and not venturing off marked trails. Swimming in the Boiling Lake in Morne Trois Pitons National Park is prohibited.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Dominica?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not. Citizens of the United States, the Commonwealth, CARICOM and several EU countries may stay up to six months, and those of the UK, France, Germany, China and about twenty others up to three. Anyone else visiting as a bona fide tourist with a return ticket may stay up to 21 days without a visa; for longer, apply for a visitor visa in advance.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Dominica?
faq.answer: It depends on your nationality: up to six months for the US, Commonwealth, CARICOM and several EU countries, up to three months for the UK, France, Germany, China and about twenty others, and up to 21 days for any other bona fide tourist with a return ticket. The Immigration Division in Roseau handles extensions.

faq.question: Is Dominica the same as the Dominican Republic?
faq.answer: No. The Commonwealth of Dominica and the Dominican Republic are different countries with separate entry rules; this page covers the Commonwealth of Dominica.

faq.question: Do I need a return ticket for Dominica?
faq.answer: Yes. Visitors are expected to hold a confirmed onward or return ticket and to give the address where they will stay.

faq.question: Can I work remotely from Dominica?
faq.answer: No official source we could read describes a remote-work visa for Dominica.
